subject: Daz
fact: Daz is leading the group through another ritual targeting a demon, having witnessed the successful use of the ritual by the Drow. He observes the acrid stench of brimstone, eerie campfire atmosphere, and five Derro chanting in harmony. He identifies the central statue as a two-headed stone giant and correctly links it to a prior encounter with a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. He cautions Thorin against rushing in and notes the ritual’s source: a book in the chief cultist’s hands. He later hears the chant invoking Demogorgon and recognizes the ritual’s intent: grafting additional heads. He is aware that Grygum’s spells are nearly ready and that Hgraam may reverse the effects on Stone Giants. He is amused when Zalthir misunderstands the size of the statue, realizing it is only two feet tall.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is meditating when interrupted by a Myconid who insists on talking to Rump-a-dump, a dissatisfied member of her circle. The Myconid claims Rump-a-dump is connected to a prior group of ape-like creatures and insists no one should be killed because they are like her. Zalthir feigns ignorance, attempts to postpone the matter, and grows frustrated as the Myconid persists, claiming he never listens. The Myconid reveals their ability to convert dead enemies into zombies, alarming Zalthir. He warns he does not wish to become one. The Myconid becomes emotional, accusing him of not helping her friends. Zalthir, seeking quiet, invokes parental wisdom to calm the situation, and the Myconid falls asleep. He reflects on parental complaints while observing her slumber.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum prepares to pray when Pelek, now possessing a Derro body, asks to be tied up out of fear he might lose control and the Derro might kill them. Grygum is uncertain of their safety with the ghost. Daz reassures him, citing past betrayal by Buppido that resulted in a group member’s death. As they tie Pelek up, JimJar makes a bet that the knots won’t hold. The next day, Pelek remains tied, and Grygum collects his winnings. Upon untying him, Pelek reflects on the ambiguity of death and sleep, sparking a philosophical impulse in Grygum that is cut short by the need to prepare for battle. Grygum later reassures Thorin that Hgraam can handle the new two-headed stone giant statue, and their mission remains to end the cult.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a ghost possessing the body of a Derro. He fears losing control of the Derro host and requests to be restrained. He acknowledges uncertainty about whether he is truly sleeping or dead. After being tied up, he expresses relief at having had a restful night — unusual for him — and muses on the philosophical question of whether death is a form of sleep.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is eager to rush into the cultist chamber upon seeing the two-headed stone giant statue and later the Ettin. He is repeatedly cautioned by Daz and Zalthir, and he listens. He expresses concern for the safety of the giants, believing they need protection. He is displeased when told the effects on the Stone Giants might be reversed, but ultimately understands the need for patience. He points out the statue to Grygum, who reassures him Hgraam can handle it.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is a member of the group with the ability to reverse the ill effects inflicted upon Stone Giants by the cult’s ritual. Daz and Grygum both recognize this ability, and it is cited as the reason they can delay immediate action against the statue. It is implied Hgraam’s magic will mitigate the ritual’s grafting of additional heads.

subject: Myconid
fact: The Myconid is a persistent, emotionally driven creature who communicates through spores. She insists on resolving the matter of Rump-a-dump, a dissatisfied member of her circle whom she believes is being mistreated. She claims no one should be killed because the targets are like her, and reveals her kind’s ability to convert dead enemies into zombies. She becomes upset when Zalthir expresses fear of becoming one, accusing him of not helping her friends. She eventually falls asleep after Zalthir invokes parental wisdom, leaving him to reflect on her behavior.

subject: JimJar
fact: JimJar is a recurring member of the group who makes frivolous bets. He bets Grygum that the knots restraining Pelek/Derro will not hold. His behavior is described as silly, and he is present during the tying of Pelek. Grygum wins the bet the next day.

subject: Derro
fact: A Derro is present in the cultist cavern, preoccupied with a death dog and failing to notice the party’s infiltration. He is possessed by Pelek, a ghost who fears losing control of him. The Derro’s body is used as a vessel, and his actions are under the influence of Pelek’s consciousness. He is restrained with knots that hold, as confirmed the next day.

subject: Ettin
fact: An Ettin is present near the cult’s central platform, positioned next to the obvious boss. It is observed by Daz and mentioned as part of the ritual’s defensive or symbolic arrangement. It is not directly engaged but is noted as a significant threat in the chamber.

subject: Death Dog
fact: A death dog is present in the cultist cavern, distracting a Derro who is desperately trying not to be noticed. The party successfully sneaks past because the Derro is occupied with the creature, allowing them to enter undetected.

subject: Stone Giant (two-headed statue)
fact: A statue of a two-headed stone giant, two feet tall, stands at the center of the ritual platform. It is the focal point of the cult’s summoning ritual, which seeks to graft additional heads onto Stone Giants. Daz and Grygum link it to a prior encounter with a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. It is not alive but represents the ritual’s intended effect.

subject: Book in chief cultist’s hands
fact: A book held by the chief cultist is the source of the ritual chant used to summon Demogorgon and graft additional heads onto Stone Giants. Daz identifies it as the origin of the incantation, and Grygum later confirms its role in the cult’s magic.

subject: Ritual of Demogorgon
fact: The cult performs a ritual invoking Demogorgon using a chant that demands the grafting of additional heads onto Stone Giants. The ritual’s effects are believed to have altered a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. The chant is sourced from a book, and its success is implied by the presence of the statue and the Derro’s chanting. The group observes the ritual but delays intervention, trusting Hgraam to reverse its effects.

subject: Rump-a-dump’s fate
fact: The Myconid insists that Rump-a-dump, a member of her circle, is unhappy and needs to be retrieved. She claims Rump-a-dump is connected to a prior group of ape-like creatures and that no one should be killed because the targets are like her. Zalthir postpones the matter, but the Myconid remains emotionally fixated. The thread remains unresolved, with Zalthir uncertain whether the Myconids are friends or foes, and whether Rump-a-dump is a victim, a traitor, or something else.

subject: Pelek’s identity and control
fact: Pelek is a ghost possessing a Derro body and fears losing control of the host. The group ties him up as a precaution after a past betrayal led to a member’s death. Pelek questions whether death is a form of sleep, and his true intentions remain ambiguous. The thread remains open: is Pelek a trustworthy ally, a hidden threat, or something beyond comprehension?

subject: Cultist Cavern
fact: The cultist cavern is the site of repeated ritual activity targeting Demogorgon and the grafting of heads onto Stone Giants. It contains a central platform with a two-headed stone giant statue, five chanting Derro, an Ettin, a death dog, and a chief cultist holding the ritual book. The party has infiltrated it stealthily multiple times, with Derro often distracted or preoccupied. It is the focal point of the current mission to end the cult.

subject: Buppido’s lair
fact: Buppido’s lair is the group’s former base, now abandoned and grim, filled with dead bones and an altar to a demonic power. It is referenced as the site of a past betrayal where Buppido killed one of their group. The group departs from here to return to the cultist cavern.

subject: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul
fact: The second day of the second tenday of Myrtul is when the group awakens to find Pelek still tied up. Grygum collects his winnings from JimJar’s bet. Pelek reflects on sleep and death. The group then departs from Buppido’s lair to re-infiltrate the cultist cavern, where they observe a distracted Derro and a new two-headed stone giant statue.

subject: Nature of death and sleep
fact: Pelek muses on whether death is a form of sleep, sparking philosophical interest in Grygum. The thread remains open, as no definitive answer is provided, and the group must continue their mission. The question lingers as a thematic undercurrent, especially given Pelek’s ghostly nature and the Myconid’s zombie conversion process.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the head cultist leading a ritual to transform giants into two-headed monsters, demanding fervor and precision in chant and movement; he is the emotional and magical core of the Derro cult, and his madness drives their actions.
source_quote: Hear me, you two-headed fools! His madness flows, our city drools! From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn! For Demogorgon, the city will burn! More heads for grafting! More for the pile!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of the Ember Vanguard who uses darkness magic to obscure the battlefield, coordinates attacks with the party, and employs tactical repositioning to counter magical effects; he is observant and decisive in combat.
source_quote: I want to watch!", "Let’s attack now.", "They are bunched up; it’s time to attack.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric or divine caster who channels acid through violent ritual vomiting after being attacked; he survives lethal trauma and responds with potent, unorthodox magic, suggesting deep ties to chaotic or necrotic forces.
source_quote: Grygum moaning in pain, then in incantation. There is a violent heaving. I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a member of the Ember Vanguard rendered terrified by Narrak’s fear spell; he is struck by the Ettin’s morning star while incapacitated, indicating vulnerability to psychological magic.
source_quote: the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.", "The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. Thorin looks battered.

subject: The Ettin
fact: The Ettin is a two-headed monstrosity serving as a frontline combatant for the Derro cult; it is resistant to magical damage, capable of wielding dual weapons, and is the primary target of the party’s assault.
source_quote: The Ettin points at the three of us outside of the darkness...", "The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin...", "A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a subterranean cult faction devoted to Demogorgon, performing ritualistic transformations and chants to empower their city’s doom; they are obedient to Narrak but lack discipline, requiring constant correction.
source_quote: He motions to all of the Derro to surround him...", "The Derro groan and gather around him.", "The Derro only do so half heartedly...

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a group of warriors bound by magical fear and ritual alignment with Narrak’s cult; they are susceptible to psychological manipulation and serve as both targets and unwitting enforcers of the ritual’s power.
source_quote: the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.", "They are bunched up; it’s time to attack.

subject: Demogorgon’s Influence
fact: Demogorgon’s presence manifests as madness, spiraling rituals, and physical corruption; its influence warps perception, causes acid vomiting, and empowers the cult’s rituals with terrifying, reality-bending effects.
source_quote: His madness flows, our city drools!", "Demogorgon’s madness flows through me!", "the curse spreads!

subject: Ritual of the Two-Headed
fact: A cult ritual is being performed to transform giants into two-headed monsters, involving synchronized chanting, positional alignment, and the accumulation of severed heads; failure to perform with vigor risks collapse of the ritual’s power.
source_quote: We have successfully converted another of Hgraam’s giants to a two-headed monster.", "Now we shall convert one more, and by golly, they will lay waste to Gracklstugh!

subject: Darkness Ambush
fact: Zalthir casts a magical darkness over the Derro and Ettin, obscuring vision and enabling surprise attacks; the environment becomes chaotic, with combatants striking blindly and magical effects interfering with perception.
source_quote: Zalthir and I had discussed what we should do. He plans to use his darkness...", "From inside it, Narrak shouts...

subject: Fear Spell Activation
fact: Narrak casts a fear spell using a white feather, inducing paralyzing terror in the Ember Vanguard; the spell’s effect is broken when the caster is obscured by darkness, demonstrating dependency on line of sight.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.

subject: Acid Vomiting Ritual
fact: Grygum undergoes a violent physical transformation after being struck, vomiting a wave of acid—a non-spell, ritualistic manifestation of inner corruption or divine perversity tied to the cult’s influence.
source_quote: Grygum moaning in pain, then in incantation. There is a violent heaving. I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid.

subject: Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp
fact: The caster uses Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp to trap Narrak in the darkness, attempting to sever the ritual’s source; the spell triggers a final curse declaration, confirming the ritual’s inevitability.
source_quote: I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where I think he is.", "Narrak screams in rage - 'You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!'

subject: Whorlstone's Depths
fact: Whorlstone's Depths is the mythic source of Demogorgon’s power, where spiraling rituals originate and madness flows upward into the cult’s city; it is referenced in chant as the origin of corruption.
source_quote: From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn!

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the cult city targeted for destruction by the ritual; it is the ultimate goal of the two-headed transformation and the locus of the cult’s apocalyptic ambitions.
source_quote: they will lay waste to Gracklstugh!

subject: White Feather
fact: The white feather is a ritual focus used by Narrak to cast fear magic; it is a symbolic tool of control, linking the caster’s will to the emotional state of the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir...

subject: The Curse Spreads
fact: A lingering, inevitable curse tied to Demogorgon is spreading through the ritual; despite attempts to disrupt it, the curse persists, suggesting the cult’s doom is not just planned but predestined.
source_quote: Narrak screams in rage - 'You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!'

subject: Invisibility to Derro
fact: The Derro fail to notice the party because they are actively avoiding detection by Narrak; this reveals a hierarchy of fear within the cult, where subordinates prioritize appeasing their leader over battlefield awareness.
source_quote: I finally understand why that Derro, who should have seen us, has not noticed us. He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak.

subject: session date
fact: This sequence occurs during an active dungeon session, with events unfolding in real-time as the party engages in combat, ritual disruption, and tactical magic use.
source_quote: I raise an eyebrow.", "I nod.", "Finally, Narrak emerges...
